One Turnkey organization ('Toban') serves both chains. Sepolia and Base

_applied: APPLIED — created 2026-06-03, last updated 2026-07-15, verified
2026-07-26 against `list_policies`.
The live copy is still named 'toban-discord-bot-mintFrom-only'.
`policyId` above is what makes the rename safe: apply-policy.sh
updates that id in place rather than matching on the (changed) name,
which would otherwise create a SECOND policy and leave the old,
broader one live. Once applied, the live name matches `policyName`
below — which is the accurate one, since the policy allows two
selectors, not just mintFrom.
_intent: Allow the bot user to sign exactly two contract writes and nothing
else:
/thx          -> mintFrom(address,address,uint256,(uint256,address)[],bytes)
selector 0x40062e89, on a ThanksToken clone
/quest submit -> submitCompletion(address,uint256,uint256)
selector 0x947ec45f, on a HatsQuestModule clone
The gates, and why each one is here:
activity.type == SIGN_TRANSACTION_V2
Every other gate reads `eth.tx.*`, which Turnkey only populates
when the TEE parses a transaction. ACTIVITY_TYPE_SIGN_RAW_PAYLOAD_V2
(what viem's signMessage / signTypedData would use) exposes only an
opaque 32-byte hash, so none of the gates below could apply. Pinning
the activity type means any future raw-payload signing needs an
explicit, PR-reviewed policy change. `signer/turnkey.ts` already
routes production signing through sign_transaction for this reason.
eth.tx.chain_id
Confines this policy to one chain, so a leaked stamper cannot
replay the same selectors against the other deployment.
eth.tx.value == 0
Both functions are non-payable; refusing value stops a bug or an
attacker from draining the signer's gas balance.
eth.tx.data[0..10]
Function selector. `data[0..10]` is the documented Turnkey
spelling (10 hex chars = '0x' + 4 bytes).
If either selector ever changes — including a change to the RelatedRole
struct in mintFrom — recompute it and update BOTH this file and the ABI
fragment in `src/chain.ts`, which is this package's only ABI.

_decisions: Toban deploys a ThanksToken and a HatsQuestModule clone PER WORKSPACE, so
the set of legitimate targets grows every time anyone creates a workspace.
Pinning `to` would mean an update_policy call on every workspace creation,
and Turnkey's policy language cannot reference an externally maintained
address set — there is no `tag()` function; user and private-key tags tag
Turnkey resources, not Ethereum addresses. A gate that has to be edited on
every workspace creation is a gate that will be wrong most of the time, so
the selector + value + chain_id gates carry the weight instead.
Residual risk, stated so it is not mistaken for a guarantee: a leaked
stamper can invoke either selector against any contract on the pinned
chain. What still bounds it — `value == 0` stops the signer's gas balance
being drained; both calls revert on contracts that do not implement that
selector; and on a real ThanksToken the mint is capped per user by the
on-chain `mintAllowance` they granted. So the blast radius is 'mint or
submit against a Toban-shaped contract', not 'arbitrary transaction'.
If this is ever revisited, the cheap version is routing both writes
through one per-chain Toban router contract and pinning `to` to it — one
static address instead of a growing set.
